main_text.l: In hac vero re idem summus philosophus dicit, melius habuisse hunc magistratum Carthaginensem, quàm ephoros Laconicos, quòd hi è cujusvis sortis hominibus, centum-viri autem ex optimis quibusque ({ἐφόρως μὲν ἐκ τῶν τυχόντων, τὰς δὲ τὰς ἐκ τῶν ἀρίστων αἱρεθέντες [?]}) electi fuerint: quod ipsum sane ad aristocraticam rationem quoque propius accedit. Nec multò post subjicit ibidem hanc sententiam: {μεγάλων γὰρ κύεμοι [?] ἡρξεμένες [?], οὐ δύτελεῖς ὦσι, μεγάλα βλάπτειν [?], ἢ ἐλαυφων [?] ἤδη τὴν πόλιν τῶν Λακεδαιμονίων}: homines tenues ad magnam potestatem provecti multum nocent, & jam nocuére civitati Lacedaemoniorum. Atque hos Centum-viros judices illos fuisse, in quorum tribunalibus Suffetes tempore Annibalis præ-torum more actionem dirigentes sederint, de quibus Livius decad. iiii libro iiii scripsit, verisimillimum existimo. Morum quoque præfectos Carthagi-nem habuisse, cum res ejus florerent, ÆmiliusProbus nos docet. Sic enim scribit in vita Amil-care adolescens illustris & formosus As-drubal, quem nonnulli diligi turpius quàm par erat, ab eo loquebantur: nec immaledici [?] tanto viro deesse potue-rant.

page.notes: Greek passages are only partly legible at this scan resolution; the Greek letters marked [?] are best readings. The line "immaledici" may be "im maledici" with a space; I have kept it as one word, marked [?]. "ÆmiliusProbus" is printed without a space. The "e" in "potuerant" and the accent on "nocuére" are as printed. Hyphenated line-end words are kept with their printed hyphens.
